blocks.md:
In Korean, **-아/어 보다** literally means *“to do and see”* → **“to try doing something”**.

- In invitations or recommendations: *“Give it a try!”* *(먹어 보세요 = Please try eating it)*
- In the past tense: *“I have tried it”* *(먹어 봤어요 = I tried eating it)*

Conjugation follows vowel harmony:
- Stem in **ㅏ, ㅗ** → **-아 보다** *(가다 → 가 보다)*
- Other vowels → **-어 보다** *(먹다 → 먹어 보다, 입다 → 입어 보다)*
- **하다** verbs → **해 보다** *(공부하다 → 공부해 보다)*

items.tip: I have been to Jeju Island.

blocks.q: How do you ask "Have you tried eating kimchi?"
blocks.why: -아/어 보다 means "to try doing": 먹- + -어 봤어요? = 먹어 봤어요?

blocks.sentence: 이 신발이 아주 예뻐요. 한번 [신어 보세요].
blocks.meaning: These shoes are very pretty. Please try them on.
blocks.why: 신다 (to put on shoes) + -어 보세요 = 신어 보세요 (Please try them on).

blocks.q: Put in order: "I want to try going to Korea once."

blocks.hint: 먹다 has the vowel ㅓ, so it takes -어: 먹어 봤어요
blocks.why: To say you tried eating food, use 먹어 봤어요: 불고기를 먹어 봤어요.

blocks.q: Have you tried eating Korean food?

blocks.say: 한국 음식 먹어 봤어요? 정말 맛있어요.

title.en: Lesson 2. Life Experience: -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 / 없다

blocks.md:
While **-아/어 봤어요** talks about casually trying something, **-(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 / 없다** refers to whether an event has ever happened in your life (*“I have had the experience of...”* or *“I have never...”*):

- Stem without batchim → **-ㄴ 적이 있다/없다** *(가다 → 간 적이 있어요)*
- Stem with batchim → **-은 적이 있다/없다** *(먹다 → 먹은 적이 있어요)*

**The ㄹ Rule**: Stems ending in **ㄹ** drop the ㄹ: **살다 → 산 적이 있어요**, **만들다 → 만든 적이 있어요**!

items.tip: I have been to Seoul before.
I have never ridden skis before.
I have worn a Hanbok before.

blocks.q: How do you say "I have never ridden a horse"? (말을 타다 = ride a horse)
blocks.why: 타다 has no batchim, so attach -ㄴ 적이 없어요: 탄 적이 없어요.

blocks.meaning: I have been to Seoul before.
blocks.why: 가다 + -ㄴ 적이 있어요 = 간 적이 있어요 (I have had the experience of going).

blocks.q: Put in order: "I have never skied."

blocks.hint: ㄹ batchim verbs drop the ㄹ: 살다 → 산 적이 있어요
blocks.why: Verbs ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ: 살다 becomes 산 적이 있어요.

blocks.q: I have never eaten spicy food.
blocks.hint: 매운 음식(을), 먹다 → 먹은 적이 없어요

title.en: Lesson 3. Putting It Together: -아/어 본 적이 있어요

blocks.md:
In real daily conversation, native speakers combine both patterns into **-아/어 본 적이 있다 / 없다** (*“Have you ever tried doing...”*):

- **가 본 적이 있어요?** *(Have you ever been there?)*
- **먹어 본 적이 없어요.** *(I have never tried eating that.)*

It sounds softer and more natural than either pattern alone!

items.tip: Have you ever been to Jeju Island?

items.ch: 한 번도 먹어 본 적이 없어요.
items.tip: I have never even once tried eating it.
I have watched a Korean movie before.

blocks.q: A: "제주도에 가 본 적이 있어요?" How do you answer "No, I have never been there"?
blocks.why: To express never having experienced it, use 가 본 적이 없어요.

blocks.meaning: I have watched Korean dramas before.
blocks.why: 보다 + -ㄴ 적이 있어요 = 본 적이 있어요.

blocks.wrong: 한 번도 김치를 먹아 본 적이 없어요.
answers: 한 번도 김치를 먹어 본 적이 없어요.
한 번도 김치를 먹어 본 적이 없어요
blocks.hint: 먹다 takes -어 보다: 먹어 본 적이 없어요
blocks.why: 먹다 conjugates with -어: 먹어 본 적이 없어요.

blocks.q: Have you ever been to Jeju Island?
blocks.hint: 제주도에, 가 보다 → 가 본 적이 있어요?

blocks.say: 제주도에 가 본 적이 있어요? 네, 가 봤어요.

blocks.md:
Now that you can talk about your own experiences with **-아/어 봤어요**, how do you recommend that someone else try something?

Attach **-아/어 보세요** (*“Please try doing...”* or *“Why don't you try...”*):

- Bright vowels (ㅏ, ㅗ) → **-아 보세요** *(가다 → 가 보세요)*
- Dark vowels (others) → **-어 보세요** *(먹다 → 먹어 보세요, 읽다 → 읽어 보세요)*
- 하다 verbs → **해 보세요** *(공부하다 → 공부해 보세요)*

It is often paired with **한번** (*once / give it a try*) or **꼭** (*definitely*)!

items.tip: Please give this song a listen.

items.ch: 한국에 가면 제주도에 꼭 가 보세요.
items.tip: If you go to Korea, definitely visit Jeju Island.

blocks.q: Your friend hasn't tried Korean bibimbap yet. How do you warmly say: "Try eating it once"?
blocks.why: To recommend trying something to someone else, use -아/어 보세요. 먹다 takes -어 보세요 → 먹어 보세요.

blocks.sentence: 이 책이 정말 재미있어요. 한번 [읽어 보세요].
blocks.meaning: This book is really fun. Please try reading it once.
blocks.why: When suggesting someone try an activity, use -아/어 보세요. 읽다 + -어 보세요 = 읽어 보세요.

blocks.q: 듣다 (to listen) / Recommend to your friend: 「이 노래 한번 ___ . (Please try listening)」
blocks.why: 듣다 is a ㄷ-irregular verb: ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel, so 듣다 + -어 보세요 becomes 들어 보세요.

blocks.q: Put the words in order: "Definitely go to Jeju Island."
Which sentence is asking someone politely to try on shoes at a shoe store?
options: 사이즈가 맞는지 한번 신은 적이 있어요.
blocks.why: 신다 (to put on footwear) becomes 신어 보세요 when recommending a customer or friend try them on.

blocks.say: 한국에 오면 부산에 꼭 가 보세요.
